steps.say: Losing most of the small bowel leaves too little absorptive surface for food alone. Such patients need intravenous feeding while the remaining gut adapts over months.
steps.tx: **Short bowel** (shortened gut) under **200 cm** (two hundred centimetres) with colon or under **100 cm** (one hundred centimetres) without colon causes intestinal failure needing **parenteral nutrition** (intravenous feeding), with **citrulline** (gut-mass blood marker) under **20 micromol per L** (twenty units) marking severe loss.

steps.say: Keeping the ileocaecal valve and colon slows transit and salvages fluid. Patients left with bowel in continuity therefore wean from drips faster than those with an end stoma.
steps.tx: **Ileocecal valve** (gut junction gate) and colon in continuity slow transit and salvage fluids, so jejunocolic anatomy weans faster than **end-jejunostomy** (jejunal end stoma) under **100 cm** (one hundred centimetres) of remaining small bowel after massive resection, with higher fluid and magnesium loss daily.

steps.say: Dilated bowel over three and a half centimetres can be stapled into a zigzag channel. This lengthening operation cuts parenteral need substantially in selected children and adults.
steps.tx: **STEP** (stapled zigzag lengthening), or **serial transverse enteroplasty** (sequential sideways stapling), staples dilated bowel over **3.5 cm** (three point five centimetres) into zigzag channels, lengthening by **50 percent** (fifty percent) and cutting parenteral need substantially in children with dilated remnant loops after resection.

steps.say: Very wide loops over four centimetres suit a different lengthening cut. The surgeon splits the loop lengthwise along its blood supply leaves and rejoins two narrower tubes.
steps.tx: **Bianchi** (lengthwise bowel split), or **longitudinal lengthening** (along-the-length division), splits a dilated loop over **4 cm** (four centimetres) along mesenteric leaves, doubling length while halving calibre for better transit and absorption in patients with very dilated remnant bowel and recurrent sepsis.

steps.say: A gut hormone analogue can grow villi and boost absorption. Treated patients often cut their infusion volumes within months of starting therapy.
steps.tx: **Teduglutide** (gut-growth drug), a **GLP-2** (glucagon-like peptide two) analogue at **0.05 mg per kg** (zero point zero five milligrams per kilogram) daily, grows villi and cuts parenteral volume by **20 percent** (twenty percent) or more in about two thirds of treated patients.

vis.alt: Diagram of an enterocyte showing sugar transporters moving glucose and fructose into the cell and out to capillaries.
vis.caption: Enterocyte absorption: sugar transporters that teduglutide-grown villi multiply to boost uptake. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: When veins run out and the liver fails, infusions cannot continue safely. Transplantation of the intestine then offers the only route to enteral freedom.
steps.tx: **Intestinal transplant** (replacement gut) suits irreversible failure with liver disease, **lost access** (exhausted veins) or recurrent sepsis, with **5-year** (five year) survival near **60 percent** (sixty percent) at expert centres worldwide after careful listing, lifelong immune suppression and close rejection surveillance.

steps.say: Confusion after sweet meals in short bowel patients has a chemical cause. Bacteria ferment undigested sugar into an acid that clouds thinking.
steps.tx: **D-lactic acidosis** (bacterial acid overload) with confusion after carbohydrate meals in short bowel needs thiamine, bicarbonate and antibiotics for **bacterial overgrowth** (germ excess) rather than fluids alone, with carbohydrate restriction and repeated courses when symptoms recur often afterwards in clinic.

steps.say: A fresh jejunostomy can pour out litres of fluid each day. Salt solutions by mouth plus medicines that slow the gut keep patients out of hospital.
steps.tx: **High-output stoma** (flooding stoma) over **2 L** (two litres) per day gets fluid restriction with **oral rehydration salts** (salt-sugar drink), loperamide, octreotide and proton pump inhibition to cut secretions and protect kidney function with daily weight, urine and magnesium checks in clinic.

vis.alt: Flowchart sending patients with working gut to enteral feeding and massive resection to parenteral feeding.
vis.caption: Feeding route choice: massive resection sends patients to parenteral nutrition over enteral. Credit: StewardMD.
